I've handed this to our technical specialist, who is picking it up now.

I went to get pictures of the screens and it decided to function. A few weeks ago I was moving things and unplugged it. After about a week I plugged it back in and the error message began. I waited for the upgraded power supply and got the same message. Then I noticed one of the fans out of place so I gently pushed it back into place. Powered on and got the same message. Finally decided to ask about repair, and it works.

That fan is the likely culprit. A fan sitting out of place loads the board oddly and that's exactly the kind of thing that throws voltage protection, so seating it properly may well have cleared it.

Let it run a day or two and watch the hashrate and temps. If the error comes back, note the exact code and how long it ran first.

Fastest hands-on help is our Discord: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , post there and mention @nullhashrate (JD). Want me to keep this open in case it returns?
You can close this. I'll contact you if I have any further issues. Thank you.

Closing it out, David. If that error comes back, just reopen here.

Before you go, one thing: what made you work through the power supply and the fan yourself for a few weeks before asking us about it?
Just habit to troubleshoot as much as I can before asking for help.

Fair enough, and it paid off here.

What made the B30 the one you jumped on back in July, out of everything we had running?
Is Harlo B30 the new name for BSB?
Read the bsb b30 page

Yes, same miner. It's listed both ways depending on where you look, BSB B30 on your order and Harlo B30 in the newer branding, but it's one product and one batch. Harlo is the firmware side of the house (Harlo OS), and the naming is being lined up with it.

Nothing on your order changes because of it.
These miners are still novelty to me, and I'm learning. The miners will eventually be part of the solar project so I don't have to run the miners on the grid.

Solar is the right home for these. They run steady 24/7, so sizing is simple once you know each unit's draw, and off grid power is where home mining actually makes sense.

Our Discord is a good place to learn: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf

How big is the array you're building toward?
Five to ten year goal is 15-20kw.

That's serious headroom. Your B30 runs around 360 to 450 watts, so a 15 to 20 kW array leaves you room for a whole rack of them with plenty left for the house.

Good luck with the build, David. I'll leave this closed, and reopen it anytime if the Octaxe acts up or you want to talk sizing.
